hook: [act:hushed, drawing us in]Long before anyone wrote a ^word, people were already leaving ^marks. [act:wonder, painting the picture]A zigzag on a ^shell, dots beside a horse, holes dug into a ^mountain. [act:the big question][tune:rise]What were they trying to ^say? [act:bright, rolling up sleeves][tune:fall]Let's investigate ^four of them, one by ^one.

cases.t1: [act:storytelling, like a guide]First stop: ^Java, where Homo erectus cut a ^zigzag into a mussel shell, at least four hundred and thirty thousand years ago.
cases.t3: [act:explaining]Modern tools show it was cut on ^purpose. [act:the catch, light]But a ^doodle is on purpose too.
cases.t4: [act:weighing it][tune:fall]Symbols before our ^species: *plausible*. [act:gentle][tune:fall]One zigzag doesn't make a ^pattern.

cases.t1: [act:storytelling]Next: dots beside Ice Age ^paintings, and thousands of ^signs on small objects@noun.
cases.t2: [act:the bold idea, fair][tune:rise]A hunters' ^calendar, counting the months, as one team ^argues?
cases.t3: [p:0.9][act:explaining]A {2026|twenty twenty-six} study found them as ^structured as early proto-writing. [act:the catch, the analogy]But any big pile of marks holds ^patterns, like faces in ^clouds.
cases.t4: [act:weighing it][tune:fall]Marks that stored ^information: *plausible*. [act:crisp][tune:fall]What they record@verb, nobody has ^shown.

cases.t1: [act:storytelling]Next: hand stencils, ^spirals, even ^'handbags', on every inhabited ^continent.
cases.t2: [act:the challenger, fair][tune:rise]Handed down from ^one lost tradition, as Graham Hancock ^suggests?
cases.t3: [act:the analogy]One source would leave a trail, like ^footprints. [act:the twist]Instead: scattered ^dates, and brains that see spirals by themselves, on the edge of ^sleep.
cases.t4: [act:weighing it][tune:fall]One lost source: *awaiting ^evidence*. [act:warm]One shared human ^brain explains most of it.

cases.t1: [act:storytelling]Last stop: Monte Sierpe, in ^Peru: five thousand two hundred holes, snaking along a desert@noun ^ridge.
cases.t3: [act:the evidence, bright]Drones found repeating ^counts, and inside, pollen of ^maize and basket reeds. [act:the analogy]Their reading: a market, counting goods hole by hole, like eggs in a ^box.
cases.t4: [act:weighing it][tune:fall]A giant counting ^device: *plausible*, on one date so ^far.

close: [act:stepping back, calm]So, what do our four cases say ^together?
[act:clear, warm]Our own species was making symbols more than seventy thousand years ^ago, and long before writing, people were ^marking and ^counting.
